item.title: VPD officers recognized with rank promotions
item.description: Valley council promotes three police officers to captain, buys 8.2-acre Fob James Dr. tract and approves first Community Center membership rate hike under Mayor Riley.

item.description: “Mama, why do all the people who look like Ruth live in one section of town?” I asked after we drove Miss Ruth home. “I don’t know, honey, but it’s always been this way.” My mother said with a bit of sorrow in her voice. item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Bill King: The Winter Storm of ‘93
item.description: It looks like we dodged the storm down here in L.A. (Lower Alabama). Much of our nation is caught in the grip of more snow and ice than they’ve seen in a while. That includes part of the northern end of Alabama, especially the northwest corner. I am praying for all of those who have been, or will be, impacted. I give thanks that this one missed us down here. item.title: AHSAA reclassifies high school teams for next school year
item.description: AHSAA drops its seven-class system, creates separate public and private divisions, and shifts Chambers County teams into new regions for 2026-28.

item.title: LaFayette City Council explores grant writing
item.description: LaFayette council taps a consultant to demystify grant writing, tie funding to economic growth, and set 30–90 day goals aligned with its new comprehensive plan.

item.title: West Point looks to outsource new housing inspections
item.description: West Point moves to outsource all building inspections to Charles Abbott Associates at a reduced contract rate, with a council vote on the expanded agreement set for Feb. 9.

item.title: A Simple Guide to What Police Are Allowed to Do
item.description: Police make sure that laws are followed, keep the peace, and keep people safe. The law gives them authority, but it also limits what they can do.

item.title: Free food distribution set for Feb. 21
item.description: Valley Community Outreach will host a free food distribution Feb. 21, 10 a.m.–noon ET at Valley Sportsplex, first-come for Valley, West Point, Lanett and nearby residents.

item.title: BOE recognizes Amazing Shake competition winners
item.description: Chambers County BOE honors W.F. Burns Amazing Shake winners, hears proposal for a Montgomery internship, and approves staff cuts and the 2026-27 school calendar.

item.title: Margaret Scott Rollison
item.description: Margaret Scott Rollison entered into the presence of her Lord and Savior on January 26, 2026, passing peacefully at her home. She was born on March 30, 1960, in Langdale, Alabama, to William Henry Scott, Jr., and Eleanor Davis Scott. Margaret was raised in West Point, Georgia, where her faith was deeply rooted and nurtured as a lifelong member of West Point United Methodist Church.
